newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia declares anthrax victory close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia declares anthrax victory close.

text.p: The Australian state of Victoria said on Monday it was close to declaring victory over the anthrax outbreak in the Tatura-Stanhope area.
Victoria's chief veterinary officer, Andrew Turner, said no new properties had been discovered with anthrax in the four days to Sunday.
In the past week, only four new properties had been confirmed with the disease, he said.

"I believe this is a very strong indication of the success of our stratagy of vaccination and quarantine. If this continues for a few more days, we will be able to say that it is all over," Turner said in a statement.
A trade protection buffer zone created around the infected area was now more than four times the size of the properties affected, he said.
The strictest measures had been taken to guarantee the quality and safety of Victoria's food products, he said.
A total of 66,500 cows and 2,300 sheep had been vaccinated in the most extensive programme of mass vaccination of animals in an official disease control programme in Victoria in 15 years, he said.
Since the outbreak of anthrax on January 26, 83 properties in the affected area have been confirmed with anthrax, while 477 properties have been vaccinated.
A total of 190 cattle and three sheep have been confirmed as having died from the disease.
Anthrax is a bacterial disease which causes rapid death in cattle and sheep. It is rarely contracted by humans and is not passed on through processed dairy products.
